tldr: For any fixed finite pattern of sensitivity and false-positive sharing, an exact guarded graph-root procedure decides whether a selected latent risk contrast is constant over the whole oriented positive fiber at a rational compatible population table. It returns the identified algebraic value or positive observational twins; only four component roots and 16 finite-root tuples can matter. In the concrete crossed three-arm pattern, these bounds improve to three roots and eight tuples, and an exact continuous fiber identifies the contrast \(1/6\) while every risk varies. For any two-assay partition pattern with nonzero covariance at eligible arms, a compatible-table rule and finite placement optimization determine the least costly informative armwise third-assay placements for target recovery. The informative fully shared Hui--Walter case with unequal risks recovers the full oriented model, whereas an uninformative second assay gives a positive nonidentification witness in every partition superclass.
gap: Verified theorem-level comparators cover shared channels, generic informative three-view recovery, named-model elimination, or class-invariant item-covariate logit shifts. None of those inspected statements gives a global positive-fiber selected-contrast certificate for the explicit three-arm crossed pattern. The broad multigroup partial-homogeneity model of Clogg--Goodman (1984) may contain this equality submodel; its theorem text was unavailable, so no priority or non-overlap claim is based on it.
